ca_clifflet.blurb: Clifflet is a small outcrop on the far right end of the Scheelite Cliffs in Pine Creek Canyon, west of Bishop in the Eastern Sierra, and it sits among the crags nearest the canyon mouth. It has nine routes: six trad and three sport, mostly around 5.10 with a few easier lines and one 5.11. The granodiorite on the southeast face is at its best toward the left side and gets grainier as you move right. Expect technical, off-vertical climbing on patina edges, crimps and mantles. Sun hits it earlier than the neighboring walls, which suits the cooler months.

ca_cunning_rock_southeast_face.blurb: This is the sunny side of Cunning Rock, a long formation in the Jumbo Rocks area of Joshua Tree National Park, set just off the road close to the campground and a nearby picnic area. It has nine routes, eight of them trad and one sport, running from 5.7 up to a single 5.11, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.10. The monzogranite is coarse and abrasive. Morning light warms the face, so it works well on a cold day, and the short walk from the road keeps the day simple.

ca_dark_side.blurb: Dark Side is a wall on High Eagle, up in the western Sierra foothills of Shuteye Ridge at roughly 7,000 feet, close to Friend Rock camp. It holds nine routes, six sport and three trad, mostly 5.10 with a couple of 5.11s and one 5.12. The granodiorite wall faces west. The walk from camp is short and heads downhill toward an amphitheater.

ca_boulder_3_5_mist_area.blurb: This small cluster of granodiorite boulders sits at the Roads End parking area in Cedar Grove, Kings Canyon National Park, between Boulder 3 on the east side and Boulders 4 and 5 to the west. The Mist Boulder is the main attraction. There are nine problems, from very easy up to one V4, with most falling between V0 and V2. Expect low-to-the-ground lines and some slab, which makes it an easy stop alongside the larger boulder groups nearby.
